bull_bear.body: the credit rating reaffirmation may have a positive impact on the company's stock price
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance-sheet philosophy is built on an "OWNED & FULLY PAID Land Bank" described as a "Strategic land bank supporting margin resilience and capital efficiency", alongside "Efficient Capital Deployment — Prudent capital deployment and Value-Accretive Execution across the development lifecycle".
- Stated sequencing of the balance sheet: debt reduction in FY2026-27, then "Improved Cashflows" and "Cash Positive" in FY2027-28.
- Once cash positive, capital is earmarked for growth rather than return: "New Investments in JDA/JV and Land" in FY2027-28.
- "Profitability Focused — Enhanced profitability supported by sustainable, repeatable financial performance" and "Luxury-led developments offer structurally higher margins through differentiated positioning".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Owned, fully paid land bank in high-value, supply-constrained Delhi and Gurugram micro-markets, described as the base for a pipeline of GDV comparable to the entire existing portfolio
- Delivery track record: TARC Tripundra, launched in FY2023, was delivered within timeline and handovers commenced in FY26, described as a benchmark boutique luxury development in the Capital
- Experience-led selling through galleries and experience centres that build brand recall and goodwill among discerning buyers
- Design depth, product curation and experiential selling cited as areas where the Company holds a genuine edge against larger national developers entering NCR
- Green-building credentials — two of three projects certified LEED Gold / LEED Platinum, with alignment to LEED, IGBC and GRIHA standards
- Integrated IT systems including Farvision ERP for construction progress, budget and vendor tracking, enabling real-time monitoring and data-driven decision-making
- Internal control framework with periodic internal audits by an independent audit firm reporting to the Audit Committee, considered adequate and effective in FY26
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Occupational health and safety at construction sites — Flagged as a material issue: construction and real estate operations inherently involve exposure to workplace hazards that may lead to occupational injuries, ill-health, fatalities, operational disruptions, project delays and legal liabilities, and can affect stakeholder confidence and corporate reputation. Mitigated through recognised health and safety standards, internal audits, training, hazard identification and a stated "Zero Harm" commitment.
- Regulatory compliance across a highly regulated development environment — Evolving legal and regulatory requirements across real estate development, environmental management, labour practices and governance may increase compliance complexity and regulatory exposure, with financial penalties, litigation risk, project delays and reputational impact from non-compliance. Managed through proactive monitoring, periodic compliance reviews and internal audits.
- Climate change and physical resilience of projects — Increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events, rising temperatures, changing climatic conditions, resource constraints and evolving climate-related regulations may affect project execution and asset performance (the disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the source text).
- Data protection, privacy and cybersecurity — Increasing digitisation, technology-enabled operations and a growing volume of customer data heighten exposure to cybersecurity threats, unauthorised access and data breaches, which may disrupt business continuity and trigger regulatory penalties, financial loss and reputational damage.
- Talent attraction, retention and workforce capability — Failure to attract, retain and develop talent, combined with evolving workforce expectations, technology-driven skill gaps and disengagement, may materially impact productivity, operational effectiveness and overall business performance; attrition also raises recruitment and training costs.
- Human rights and ethical conduct across operations and the value chain — Human rights violations within operations or the value chain, ethical misconduct and regulatory non-compliance may cause reputational damage, erosion of stakeholder trust, legal liabilities and adverse business outcomes; addressed through the governance framework, compliance training and grievance mechanisms.
- Concentration in a single segment and a single geography — The Directors' Report describes the portfolio as luxury and ultra-luxury developments across New Delhi and Gurugram only, so the business depends on one product segment in one metropolitan market and on a fully paid-up strategic land bank there; the disclosed material-issues table contains no separate concentration mitigation.
- Macro and geopolitical headwinds affecting luxury demand and input costs — The US-Israel-Iran conflict is expected to cut FY27 GDP growth to 6.6% from a pre-conflict 7.2% and add roughly 90 bps to inflation, with a prolonged disruption to shipping or energy infrastructure the key downside risk. Rupee depreciation raises the cost of imported construction materials and fittings, and Gulf economies - nearly 38% of India's remittances - are a meaningful source of NRI ultra-luxury demand that any labour-market disruption there would hit.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Strategic focus is deliberately narrow: "NEW DELHI & GURUGRAM", described as "Delhi & Gurugram: India's Luxury Epicentre", with a stated "HIGH-MARGIN Business Model", "OWNED & FULLY PAID Land Bank" and "EXECUTION and DELIVERY FOCUS".
- The market thesis rests on scarcity: "Delhi's urban core has near-zero developable land. High barriers to entry limit new supply, sustaining strong pricing power and long-term appreciation in well located micro markets", with "the ultra-luxury segment in Delhi remains significantly underserved despite rising demand".
- Demand base framed as "HNIs, business families, senior professionals and NRIs seeking premium lifestyle offerings and long-term asset security in the Capital".
- "Superior Economics": the ultra-luxury segment is said to benefit from "strong realizations, healthy margins, calibrated monetization and robust cashflow visibility".
- Brand validation cited via awards: Asia One India's Greatest Brands 2023-24 and Times Realty Luxury Project of the Year 2024 (TARC Kailasa), ET Real Estate Awards 2025 Residential Ultra Premium (TARC Ishva), and Forbes India A-List Developer 2025.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Auditor change] "we have appointed Singhi & Co., among India's Top 10 audit firms, as the Company's Statutory Auditor", framed by the CEO as reinforcing transparency, financial discipline and governance standards.
- [Deck contradiction] The CEO statement reads "FY2026 Consolidated revenue stood at ₹218.7 crore, with PAT of ₹22.64 crore", yet the identical figures are labelled Q1 FY2027 on the financial-highlights and snapshot pages — the deck applies two different period labels to the same numbers.
- [Leadership] Promoter-led board — Mr. Anil Sarin (Founder & Chairman), Mr. Amar Sarin (Managing Director & CEO), Ms. Muskaan Sarin (Whole Time Director & Chief Brand Officer) — with four independent directors drawn from banking, company-secretarial and audit backgrounds.
- [Segment view] "The luxury housing segment is undergoing a meaningful evolution, with discerning buyers increasingly seeking residences that combine architectural distinction, thoughtful design and a differentiated lifestyle experience" — presented as the opportunity for developers able to curate and execute consistently.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: TARC develops luxury and ultra-luxury residential projects in Delhi and Gurugram, anchored in curated living, design excellence, execution discipline and owned land parcels in high-value micro-markets. It sells to discerning HNI/UHNI homebuyers in the capital region through experience-led selling at its galleries and experience centres, and its brand-led approach and focus on quality construction position it to benefit from the structural premiumisation of residential demand. In FY26 revenue recognition and customer handovers commenced at TARC Tripundra while sales momentum was sustained across TARC Kailasa and TARC Ishva.

business.title: Quality certifications

outlook.body:
- Concentrate the entire strategic footprint on Delhi and Gurugram — described as the most established and supply-constrained property markets in India — where the Company's knowledge, relationships and heritage run deepest
- Develop a fully owned land bank across Delhi and Haryana acquired at historical cost, which provides the base for a development pipeline of comparable scale to what is currently under execution
- Launch multiple new projects, already through design finalisation with approvals in place, in a phased and disciplined sequenced rollout
- Anchor the financial strategy in deleveraging toward a debt-free balance sheet so that expansion remains self-sustaining and value-accretive
- Shift borrowings from structured, higher-cost debt into conventional bank and NBFC facilities at better rates, and link borrowings directly to active developments so repayments are serviced from those projects' customer collections
- Orient sales toward genuine end-user residents building primary homes rather than speculative inventory-led selling, which supports collections quality and payment discipline
- Use the immersive preview model — dedicated experience centres with full-scale sample residences at Kailasa and Ishva — as the primary conversion tool to shorten the decision cycle
- Differentiate on product: four-sided open residences, generous private decks, wellness-oriented amenities and spacious layouts, with pricing that reflects that differentiation
- Advance a forward pipeline of three new developments in advanced stages of design and regulatory clearance, each conceived on the same principles as the existing portfolio
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TARC's expansion is a residential development pipeline rather than plant capex. The Company reports a pipeline under finalisation with GDV comparable to its entire existing portfolio — TARC V (1 million sq ft, 7 acres), TARC VI (0.5 million sq ft, 3 acres) and TARC VII (1 million sq ft, 7 acres) — all on owned, fully paid land with approvals in place and design finalisation underway; it has indicated that JDA, JV and new investment activity will commence as the balance sheet moves toward becoming cash positive. The Directors' Report states that TARC is actively advancing a significant pipeline of luxury and ultra-luxury developments with design finalisation underway across multiple projects planned for launch over the coming years, supported by a fully paid-up strategic land bank and a scalable development platform. Every development is designed to meet green certification standards: TARC Ishva and TARC Kailasa have both received IGBC Platinum pre-certification and TARC Tripundra holds IGBC Gold pre-certification, against a stated target of a 100% green-certified portfolio. On the execution side the Company has integrated renewable energy solutions such as rooftop solar power, solar street lighting and solar water heating systems wherever feasible, and adopted smart MEP systems with sensor-based monitoring, prefabricated and modular construction techniques and Building Information Modelling; it states that project-specific investments have been made to improve energy performance but that the capital expenditure attributable to energy conservation cannot be separately quantified because those initiatives are integrated into overall project execution. No imported technology was introduced during the year, and R&D expenditure is not separately identifiable.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Reported revenue is recognised under Ind AS 115 on the project completion method (income only on achieving occupancy milestones), so operating cash from customer collections runs ahead of the P&L and reported earnings converge with cash as projects complete
- Earnings trajectory expected to steepen as Kailasa and Ishva reach completion milestones over the next three to four years and enter their recognition cycles
- Margin profile on future recognition supported by the cost basis of owned land, creating a favourable spread between development cost and realisation price
- Structural premiumisation of Indian residential demand: the ₹1 crore-plus segment recorded 1,75,091 sales in 2025, up 14% YoY and 50% of total transactions versus nearly 13% in 2022, while sub-₹50 lakh sales fell 17%
- NCR led all major markets on weighted-average price appreciation at +19% YoY in 2025, on premium and luxury launches in Gurugram, Noida and Greater Noida
- Expanding ultra-wealthy base: individuals with net worth above USD 30 million rose 63% between 2021 and 2026, with a further 27% rise forecast by 2031
- Easier monetary conditions — RBI cut the repo rate by a cumulative 125 bps to 5.25% — improved homebuyer sentiment, affordability perceptions and credit conditions
- Demand held up in upper-ticket categories even as the market entered 2026 in consolidation: sales above ₹1 crore grew 11% YoY, with ₹2–5 crore and ₹10–20 crore up 17% and 12%
- INR depreciation cuts both ways for ultra-luxury developers — raising the cost of imported construction materials and fittings while making Indian assets more attractively priced for NRI buyers
- FY27 GDP growth projected at 6.6%, revised down from a pre-conflict 7.2% on higher energy prices and uncertainty, recovering to 7.2% in FY28 assuming normalisation
- Gulf economies account for nearly 38% of India's remittances and Gulf NRI buyers are a meaningful ultra-luxury demand segment, so labour-market disruption there is a downside risk
- Pre-sales bookings of ₹1,373 crore and customer collections of ₹799 crore in FY26, with operating cash generation of ₹1,132 crore
- TARC Kailasa pre-sales bookings of ₹521 crore for the year, with premium tower inventory attracting buyers at a higher price point
- TARC Ishva pre-sales bookings of ₹852 crore with customer collections of ₹411 crore, a collections-to-pre-sales ratio of 48% for the year
- TARC Tripundra generated customer collections of ₹266 crore during the year and delivered embedded gross margin of approximately 45% at the project level
- Approximately ₹730 crore remains to be recognised from Tripundra in FY27, following the ~₹270 crore already recognised in FY26
- Ishva's development potential was enhanced from approximately ₹2,700 crore to ₹3,600 crore across six towers and 518 residences spanning 1.7 million square feet after regulatory approval for an additional phase and the introduction of Ishvara
- Kailasa (₹4,400 crore GDV) and Ishva (₹3,600 crore GDV) together carry development potential of approximately ₹8,000 crore
- The three developments together carry approximately ₹9,000 crore in total development potential, with the bulk of customer collections and accounting recognition still ahead
- Q1 FY27 pre-sales bookings of ₹602 crore, a threefold increase year-on-year, and customer collections of ₹305 crore, 80% growth over Q1 FY26
- A pipeline of comparable scale beyond the current portfolio: three new developments in advanced stages of design and regulatory clearance

deepdive.thesis: TARC Limited's credit rating has been reaffirmed by Infomerics Valuation and Rating Limited with a rating of IVRBBB- and a stable outlook, indicating a moderate level of creditworthiness. The reaffirmation of the credit rating is expected to have a positive impact on the company's ability to raise debt capital in the future.

risks.note: Human rights violations within operations or the value chain, ethical misconduct and regulatory non-compliance may cause reputational damage, erosion of stakeholder trust, legal liabilities and adverse business outcomes; addressed through the governance framework, compliance training and grievance mechanisms.
risks.risk: Human rights and ethical conduct across operations and the value chain

risks.note: The Directors' Report describes the portfolio as luxury and ultra-luxury developments across New Delhi and Gurugram only, so the business depends on one product segment in one metropolitan market and on a fully paid-up strategic land bank there; the disclosed material-issues table contains no separate concentration mitigation.
risks.risk: Concentration in a single segment and a single geography

risks.note: The US-Israel-Iran conflict is expected to cut FY27 GDP growth to 6.6% from a pre-conflict 7.2% and add roughly 90 bps to inflation, with a prolonged disruption to shipping or energy infrastructure the key downside risk. Rupee depreciation raises the cost of imported construction materials and fittings, and Gulf economies - nearly 38% of India's remittances - are a meaningful source of NRI ultra-luxury demand that any labour-market disruption there would hit.
risks.risk: Macro and geopolitical headwinds affecting luxury demand and input costs
